name: Bhakti-yoga: loving meditation (upāsana, dhruvānusmṛti)
method_summary: Daily, repeated meditation on the Lord (in one of the Upaniṣadic forms, the vidyās) as one's inner self, until it becomes unbroken, vivid as sight and full of love; supported by the seven aids and by duties done as worship, continued until death, with remembrance at the last moment.
stage: for those qualified by birth, learning and capacity (traivarṇika) after karma- and jñāna-yoga
prerequisites: karma-yoga and jñāna-yoga leading to the vision of the self

warnings.text: It is long and difficult, obstructed by accumulated sins, and requires the last remembrance at death; hence prapatti is taught for those unable.

name: The Upaniṣadic meditations (brahma-vidyās)
method_summary: Specific forms of meditation on Brahman taught in the Upaniṣads (such as the Dahara, Śāṇḍilya, Madhu and Antarākṣi vidyās), traditionally counted as thirty-two; each is a form of bhakti-yoga, chosen and practised according to the rules of the Brahma Sūtras' third chapter.
notes: The count of thirty-two and the list are recalled with low confidence.

name: Surrender (prapatti / śaraṇāgati) in the Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition
method_summary: Taking refuge, once and for all, at the feet of Nārāyaṇa with Śrī as the sole means, through a teacher, typically by reciting the dvaya: with resolve to please, avoidance of displeasing, great faith, choosing him as protector, helplessness, and laying down the burden of one's protection; thereafter living in service, free from anxiety about salvation. The Vaṭakalai treat it as a means performed; the Teṅkalai as acceptance of the Lord as the means.
stage: open to all, of any class or gender
signs_of_progress: freedom from anxiety (the Lord's 'do not grieve')

equivalents.note: the same six-limbed surrender of the Pāñcarātra (U08)

warnings.text: To regard one's own surrender as the means is a fault (Teṅkalai).
Surrender must not be repeated as a means; repetition is allowed only as expiation (Vaṭakalai).

name: Bharanyāsa: the rite of laying down one's burden
method_summary: The formal performance of surrender, in which one places the burden of one's protection and its fruit on the Lord, with the sāttvika-tyāga; performed by oneself, by repeating after the teacher, or by the teacher on one's behalf.

name: The five sacraments (pañcasaṃskāra, samāśrayaṇa)
method_summary: Śrīvaiṣṇava initiation by the teacher: the marks of discus and conch on the shoulders (tāpa), the upright forehead mark (puṇḍra), a servant-name (nāma), the three secret mantras (mantra) and instruction in worship (yāga). Summary only.
notes: U14's contribution to U08's entry; Rāmānuja received it from Periya Nambi at Madhurāntakam.

name: The fivefold daily routine (pañcakāla)
method_summary: The day divided into five periods: approach (abhigamana), gathering materials (upādāna), worship (ijyā), study (svādhyāya) and meditation (yoga), as practised by Śrīvaiṣṇavas following the Pāñcarātra and the Nityagrantha.

name: Daily home worship of the Lord (tiruvārādhanam)
method_summary: Worship of the Lord's image (arcā) at home each day, with purification, meditation on the teachers, offerings of water, flowers, food, recitation and prostration, done as service and not for any fruit.

name: Recitation and contemplation of the tirumantra
method_summary: Repetition of 'oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya', received at initiation, with contemplation of its meaning: the soul belongs to the Lord alone, not to itself, and seeks only his service.

name: Constant recollection of the dvaya
method_summary: Reciting the dvaya with its meaning — refuge at the feet of Nārāyaṇa with Śrī, and prayer for service — throughout life, as the Lord bade Rāmānuja in the Śaraṇāgati Gadya.

name: Recitation of the Divya Prabandham
method_summary: Recitation of the Āḻvārs' hymns in temples and homes — daily selections (nityānusandhānam), the annual festival of recitation (adhyayana-utsava) and the sung and enacted araiyar service — as the Tamil Veda.

name: Service (kainkarya) to the Lord
method_summary: Service of the Lord in temple and home — making garlands, cleaning, cooking offerings, singing — done for his pleasure alone, the natural expression of the soul's being his servant.

name: Service to devotees (bhāgavata-kainkarya)
method_summary: Honouring and serving the Lord's devotees regardless of their birth, which the teachers rank above service to the Lord himself; avoiding any offence against them.

name: Pilgrimage to the divine sites and maṅgaḷāśāsana
method_summary: Visiting the temples sung by the Āḻvārs and praying for the Lord's welfare there, as the Āḻvārs and teachers did.

name: Relinquishment before action (sāttvika-tyāga)
method_summary: Before any act, relinquishing the sense of agency, of ownership and desire for its fruit: 'the Lord himself, for his own sake, has this done through me'.

name: The seven aids as disciplines
method_summary: Purity of food, freedom from desire, repeated practice, performance of the five great sacrifices and other duties, the virtues (truthfulness, uprightness, compassion, generosity, non-injury, non-covetousness), freedom from dejection and from elation.

name: Traditional study with the teacher (kālakṣepa)
method_summary: Study of the Śrībhāṣya, the Gītābhāṣya, the Tiruvāymoḻi commentaries and the rahasya works at the feet of a teacher of the lineage, orally, in the traditional order.

name: Wearing the upright mark (tirumaṇ)
method_summary: Daily application of the vertical white clay mark with the central line for Śrī on the forehead and body, a sign of belonging to the Lord.

name: Fasting on Ekādaśī
method_summary: Abstaining from grain (or food) on the eleventh lunar day as an observance pleasing to the Lord. Summary only.
